name: RF-360 passive RF sensor (Dedrone)
description: Omnidirectional passive RF sensor (Dedrone by Axon). Detects, classifies and direction-finds drones and controllers by protocol signature. 2 km is the normal-conditions figure; up to 5 km is claimed in ideal conditions against specific drones. One unit gives angle of arrival only.

detectRangeM.condition: 2000 m for most drones in normal conditions; up to 5000 m in ideal conditions

rangeAccuracyM.note: A single-site RF direction finder measures bearing, not range; not established by the public record.

azimuthAccuracyDeg.source: Dedrone RF-360 installation manual (IM-Inst-RF360en, FCC filing 2AO3N-TH87P6EROZ): '±5° (mean error)', quoted from the search index; the v2.0 datasheet carries no accuracy line

elevationAccuracyDeg.note: Two-dimensional RF direction finding gives no elevation; not established by the public record.

receiverSensitivityDbm.note: Planning factor, 2.4 GHz band, channel-integrated: kTB for a 10 MHz OcuSync-class channel (-104 dBm) plus a 12 dB receiver noise figure (Narda SignalShark C-UAS application note) gives -92 dBm, recorded as -90 dBm. Cross-check: against a 2 W (33 dBm) EIRP DJI link with a 0 dBi receive antenna this threshold falls at about 6 km free space, consistent with the RF-360 datasheet's 2 km normal to 5 km ideal. Dedrone publishes no sensitivity (RF-360 datasheet V2.0).

geolocationMinNodes.condition: angle-of-arrival localisation (datasheet); 'in combination with two or more RF-360 sensors, it is able to determine the position of a drone' (manual)
geolocationMinNodes.source: Dedrone RF-360 datasheet V2.0 (AoA) and RF-360 manual as quoted by the search index of manualslib (page returned 403)
